items.stem: What does `0 == ''` evaluate to in JavaScript, and why does `0 === ''` differ?

options.text: true for ==, false for ===, because == coerces types while === does not
options.rationale: Correct: == performs type coercion; === compares type and value without coercion.
=== is false because the types differ.

items.explanation: Correct: == performs type coercion; === compares type and value without coercion.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about closures are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A closure keeps access to variables from its defining scope
options.rationale: Correct: closures capture their lexical environment.

options.text: let in a loop creates a fresh binding per iteration
options.rationale: Correct: this fixes the classic var-in-loop capture bug.

options.text: Closures copy values at definition and never see updates
options.rationale: Closures reference variables, so they see later updates.

items.explanation: Correct: closures capture their lexical environment.

items.stem: An awaited promise rejects. How do you handle the error idiomatically?

options.rationale: Correct: try/catch around await captures a rejected promise.
Unhandled rejections do not resolve themselves.

options.text: Use a synchronous try/catch without await
options.rationale: Without await the rejection is not caught synchronously.
Re-calling does not handle the rejection.

items.explanation: Correct: try/catch around await captures a rejected promise.
